counterfactual_missing_items: Raw text does not literally state 'brown tumor' as a label, but the histologic wording is characteristic.
No explicitly disconfirming span supports primary hyperparathyroidism as the sole final diagnosis of the finger lesion.
Systemic bone changes are present in the vignette but not assigned to R3's raw_support_spans.
decisive_items: Numerous giant cells with multiple osteoclastlike nuclei and giant multinucleated cells dispersed in contact with fibers associated with small vessels.
complete lysis of the underlying phalanx and periosteal bone resorption in the phalangeal tuft band
response.rationale: R3 directly matches the lesion pathology: a fibrous, woven-bone, giant-cell-rich, brown-tinting osteolytic finger tumor is the classic histologic signature of a brown tumor complicating hyperparathyroidism. R1 matches the diffuse skeletal imaging pattern of osteitis fibrosa cystica but does not directly capture the decisive finger tumor histology; R2 only identifies an already known underlying biochemical state.

rejected.why: It is the already-stated underlying endocrine condition and its raw support does not explain the focal lytic finger tumor or giant-cell/brown histology.
